---
title: Get started
description: Install Quarto Glossary and render a first document with terms and acronyms.
---

## Requirements

- Quarto 1.4 or newer.
- Nothing else for HTML. The filter is Lua and the balloon script is plain
  JavaScript with no dependencies.
- For PDF, a TeX distribution with `glossaries` and `glossaries-extra`.
  TinyTeX installs them on demand (`quarto install tinytex`).

## Install

Run this from the root of each Quarto project:

```bash
quarto add brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary
```

Quarto copies the extension into `_extensions/brenobeirigo/glossary`. Commit
that directory with the project so every build uses the same version.
`quarto list extensions` shows the installed version.

## A first document

Create `lesson.qmd`. The vocabulary sits in the [[front-matter]], so this one
file is all you need:

```markdown
---
title: First glossary
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  entries:
    - id: metadata
      term: metadata
      definition: Structured information describing another resource.

    - id: api
      kind: acronym
      short: API
      long: application programming interface
      definition: An interface through which software components communicate.
---

The [[metadata]] are available through an [[api]]. Later, the [[api]]
returns the current record.

::: {.glossary}
:::
```

Render it:

```bash
quarto render lesson.qmd --to html
quarto render lesson.qmd --to pdf
```

The text reads:

> The [[metadata]] are available through an [[api]]. Later, the [[api]]
> returns the current record.

The first [[api|short]] reference expands. The second is abbreviated. The
placeholder prints an Acronyms list and a Glossary list with the entries the
document used.

## Move the terms to a file

When several documents share terms, move the `entries` list into
`glossary.yml` and point the documents or `_quarto.yml` at it:

```yaml
filters: [glossary]
glossary:
  path: glossary.yml
```

[Ways to define terms](define-terms.qmd) covers several files, JSON, and
websites with a shared glossary page.

## When something looks wrong

| You see | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Literal `[[key]]` in the page | The filter is not active. Add `filters: [glossary]` to the document or to `_quarto.yml`. |
| `cannot find vocabulary file 'glossary.yml'` | There is no `path` and no `entries`. Add one of them under `glossary:`. |
| `found entries: at the top level` | `entries:` must be indented under `glossary:`. |
| `unknown glossary key [[apii]] …; did you mean [[api]]?` | A misspelt key. Every unknown key in the document is listed in one message. |
| A wrong plural such as "childs" | Plurals of regular words are formed automatically. Give irregular ones a `plural:` field, or write `[[child|children]]` once. |
| No Glossary or Acronyms list | The document has no `::: {.glossary}` placeholder. Without one, terms keep their balloons but are not links. |
| `glossary warning: … unknown field 'plurl'` | A misspelt field in an entry. The warning suggests the right name. |

## Update

Run the installation command again from the project root:

```bash
quarto add brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary
```

Review and commit the changed files under `_extensions/`. The
[changelog](https://github.com/brenobeirigo/quarto-glossary/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
lists what changed in each release.
